mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year indicates inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% year-over-year indicates a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST YoY < -10%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals strengthening supply-side activity, which is bullish for the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO MoM > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically boosts equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS decreases.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a weakening labor market, which is bearish for the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which is bullish for the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS MoM > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A divergence between rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) and a stable or decreasing federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) suggests a misalignment in monetary policy, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where CPIAUCSL rises and FEDFUNDS is stable or decreases.
